source.creator: Toby de Boer (@tobydeboer), Instagram reel DeOv0aupBd_
source.transcript: i'm not even yet at my Prime / i'm not at a hundred yet / i'm still charging / They don't wanna see me Win / but i know in the end i'm winning and Regardless

method_summary: Shot cuts: consecutive-frame histogram distance + luma correlation + gradient-structure correlation (tools/cuts.py, cuts2.py), every candidate confirmed on contact sheets.

Glyph masks: iterative two-model segmentation (pixel = B or 1-B with smooth B) on tight boxes; sans masks cleaned with an Inter Display ExtraBold rendering registered to the frame (tools/textmask.py, refmask.py, rendermask.py).

Per-frame geometry: similarity registration (scale + translation) of each word's mask against every frame by normalised correlation of gradient magnitude (tools/register.py). Scores 0.8-0.99 inside a word's lifetime, <0.65 outside -> exact first/last frames.
Background motion: ORB + RANSAC similarity between consecutive frames with caption boxes masked (tools/bgmotion.py).

Blend tests: (a) edge pairs, pixel just inside a glyph vs its mirror just outside, fitted I_in = a + b*I_out per channel (difference -> a~1, b~-1; normal -> a~1, b~0) (tools/blendtest.py); (b) inpainted-background opacity fit (alpha_est.py); (c) chroma-flip test (chroma_test.py); (d) clean-plate tests for at my / Prime (prime.py); (e) 'un-difference' visual check: replacing glyph pixels by 1-I makes difference text disappear (spec_difference_evidence.png).
Entrance animation of the They block: alpha profile across thick glyph edges, background read 10-12 px outside, erf fit -> opacity and blur sigma per frame (tools/edgeprofile.py).

sans.class: bold lowercase neo-grotesk, tight tracking, all lowercase (incl. 'i', "i'm" with a straight apostrophe)
sans.best_available_match: Inter Display ExtraBold (IoU 0.84-0.91 against clean masks; Inter Display Bold 0.74-0.93, FreeSans/Liberation Bold 0.70-0.85)
sans.layout: single line, horizontally centred on x = W/2 (ink-bbox centre 0.499-0.503 W), vertically: the ascender-to-baseline box is centred on H/2 (ascender top ~499 px, baseline ~579 px); words with descenders therefore sit with their ink centre slightly lower (0.51-0.52 H)

script.class: large high-contrast formal/copperplate script, ~20-25 deg slant, hairline joins, swash capitals (P, T, W, R) with big entry loops; lowercase 'hundred' has straight looped-less ascenders
script.capitalisation: 4/5 script words get a swash capital (Prime, They, Win, Regardless); 'hundred' stays lowercase
script.size_relation_to_sans: swash capitals are ~3x the sans ascender height (250-272 px vs 80 px); script lowercase x-height is 1.1-1.3x the sans x-height (63-74 px vs 58 px)
script.layout: centred like the sans line; ink centre x 0.51-0.54 W (swash overhang pushes it right), y 0.49-0.52 H
script.font_identification: not identified; candidates to audition: a Didone copperplate script with swash caps (e.g. 'Kugile', 'Bodoni Script', 'Snell Roundhand', 'Pinyon Script', 'Great Vibes' are weaker matches)

typography.see_also: analysis/fonts_choice.json (separate font-matching step: Inter variable wght 750 opsz 32 ss07, 113.5 px, -0.075 em; Pinyon Script for the script) - consistent with the metrics measured here (x-height 58-59 px, tracking -0.07 em)
typography.outline_box_shadow: none (no stroke, no box, no drop shadow, no glow; edges are 1-px anti-aliased, sigma ~0.5-0.7 px)

blend.default: white text (#FFFFFF, 100% opacity) in Difference blend mode over the footage: out = |1 - B| = 1 - B per channel (Exclusion gives the identical result for pure white).
blend.why_it_looks_interactive: every glyph shows the photographic negative of whatever is behind it, so a hand, watch, monitor, sky edge or LED strip moving behind a letter changes the letter's colour in real time (watch face -> navy letters; skin -> light blue; red LED -> cyan; teal monitor -> salmon; bright sky -> near-black). There is NO occlusion anywhere: the text is always on top; 'even' f011-f015 and 'They' f088-f095 only look occluded because the passing object is inverted inside the letters.
blend.evidence: spec_difference_evidence.png; edge-pair fits: difference words give b = -0.75..-1.1 with a = 0.89..0.97 (e.g. know a=(0.93,0.88,0.88) b=(-1.02,-0.99,-1.01); hundred b~-0.9; in the b~-0.96); normal words give b~0 (Win a=(0.97,0.98,1.0) b=(-0.04,-0.05,-0.2); but i a=(0.98,0.99,0.99) b=(0.01,0.01,-0.02)). Words over almost-black backgrounds (yet f017-022, not f041-043, at a, still, i'm f063/f137, winning, and) cannot separate the two models numerically (both predict white) but show inverted bright objects inside the glyphs where they exist (yet/i'm f060-064: inverted laptop inside 'e' and 'm'), and belong to the same difference style.
blend.measured_effective_white: interior of difference text over black reads ~ (249,245,250) and the best |C-B| fits give C = 0.87-1.0; 'end' fits C ~ (213,222,227). Treat as white + the final grade/compression; optional: multiply text by 0.95 to match.

exceptions.Win (f111-116) and 'but i' (f117-121): Normal blend, opaque white (they stay white over the bright sky)
exceptions.at my (f023-027) and Prime (f028-036): Difference blend with a pink fill instead of white (see prime_solution)

prime_solution.best_model: Difference blend with a solid pink fill: out_c = |C_c - B_c|, C = (0.886, 0.545, 0.545) = RGB(226,139,139) = #E28B8B (at my: (0.87,0.605,0.555) = #DE9A8E; use #E28B8B for both)
prime_solution.interpretation: dark background -> light pink letters (P over the dark wall); bright background (white desk, window) -> |0.55-0.8| gives dark red/maroon and, where G/B exceed 0.55, dark teal-black strokes; this is exactly what is seen. A tint-times-inverse (T*(1-B), rmse 0.102), difference then red overlay (0.138), normal colour (0.232), exclusion (0.266), colour-blend (0.289), multiply (0.427) and screen (0.427) all fit worse. Fill is uniform (no gradient: per-region fits agree within ~0.04).
prime_solution.plates: Prime f028 vs f027 warped by the measured background similarity (s=0.9986); at my f027 vs f028; man doing push-ups and the overlapping other word excluded.

digital_zoom.finding: The captions are part of the composite that receives each shot's digital zoom: caption scale changes frame-by-frame by exactly the same factor as the footage (text vs background per-frame ratios agree within ~0.1-0.3%, e.g. f001->002 1.0278 vs 1.0257, f053->054 1.0197 vs 1.0197, f060->061 0.9594 vs 0.9595, f111->112 1.0244 vs 1.0245), and caption centroids move as if scaled about the frame centre (zoom fixed point measured at (941-966, 518-568)).
digital_zoom.renderer_rule: Render captions over the footage first (with the blend), then apply the shot's zoom to the composite: scale about frame centre (W/2, H/2), s(k) = 1 + A*(1 - exp(-k/tau)), k = frames since segment start, tau ~ 3.5-5.5 frames.
digital_zoom.pattern: Punch-in zooms (A = +11..+23%) start on the first frame of every emphasis/script word with a cut or new phrase (Prime f028, hundred f050, They f086, Win f111) and also on the very first frame (f001). Settle-out zooms (footage starts ~111-121% and eases back to 100%) on several other cuts (even/watch f011, yet f060, charging f070, know f122). Remaining shots drift +-0.1-0.3%/frame. 'Regardless' gets no punch (only -1.4% drift).

entrances_exits.default: hard cut in and hard cut out on exact frame boundaries; the next word replaces the previous on the very next frame (no gaps, no overlaps) - 16 of 28 words start exactly on a shot cut
entrances_exits.fades: No word fades except the stacked They/don't/wanna block. 'end' (f132-136) is NOT a fade: its opacity is constant (edge-profile alpha identical across frames; per-letter colours fit |C-B| with constant C ~0.85); the apparent fade-in is the blurred blue spire moving out from behind the letters (f132-133 letters over blue -> salmon, f135-136 over pale fog -> dark).
entrances_exits.they_block_entrance: staggered blur-in: each line fades in while a gaussian blur shrinks to 0. They: f086-f092 (opacity 0.20,0.29,0.41,0.56,0.76,0.80,0.93,...1.0; extra blur sigma 3.9,3.7,3.7,3.2,2.4,1.8,1.0,...0 px). don't: f090-f095 (opacity 0.08,0.18,0.52,0.80,0.94,0.93 then 1.0; blur 6.3,5.6,4.3,3.2,2.4,1.6 -> 0). wanna: f095-f096/97 (0.55, 1.0; blur 3.4, 1.5, 0.9 -> 0). Stagger = 4-5 frames (They f086, don't f090, wanna f094/95). Opacity ramps roughly linearly (ease-out at the end); first frame already ~15-20%.
entrances_exits.they_block_exit: hard cut at the shot cut f100 (all three lines together)

glitch.finding: There is no glitch effect. Per-channel registration of the text edges at the suspected frames gives R-G and B-G offsets below 0.5 px (f001 -0.12/-0.08 px, f003 -0.12/+0.27, f005 0.02/0.19, f060 0.00/0.01, f100 -0.37/-0.49 = same as non-glitch frames), no block displacement, no noise. What looks like an RGB glitch is the Difference blend inverting high-saturation objects behind the letters: the cyan LED strip shows red/orange inside 'i' and 'n' (f001-f008), the red LED shows cyan (f003-f004), a laptop/keyboard shows as a dark negative inside 'e' of yet and 'm' of i'm (f060-f064), the teal monitor shows salmon inside 'ee' of see with dark negative text lines (f100-f105). In addition, the opening frames carry the +11% punch-in zoom and the footage is on 2s with LED colour jumps every 2 frames, which reads as stutter.
glitch.how_to_reproduce: do nothing extra: render difference text over footage with saturated moving light sources; optionally hold footage frames in pairs (12 fps) for the opening stutter

emphasis_rule.observed: Script words: Prime, hundred, They, Win, Regardless = 5 of 32 spoken words (28 caption units; ~1 in 6), roughly one per spoken line, ~1 every 1.3 s. They are the payoff content word of the line (noun/number/verb/adverb, usually the last word of the phrase: Prime, hundred, Win, Regardless) or the antagonist pronoun that opens a line (They). Function words, 'i'/'i'm' and the main verb chain are never script. The last word of the video is script and is held longest (16 frames). Consecutive script words never occur back-to-back.
emphasis_rule.rule_for_new_transcript: 1) Split the transcript into spoken lines/phrases. 2) In each line pick at most one word (two only for a long contrastive line, e.g. a pronoun at the start AND the payoff at the end): prefer the final content word that completes the claim (noun, number word, strong verb, or a sentence-final adverb like 'regardless'); a subject pronoun opening an 'us vs them' line may also be picked. 3) Target ~15-20% of words (about 1 per 1-1.5 s), never function words, never two adjacent words. 4) Always make the final word of the video script. 5) Script words: swash capital initial (keep lowercase for number words like 'hundred'), ~3x height, centred (or stacked block, see below), on-screen 9-16 frames, and start a punch-in zoom of +10-13% (exp ease tau ~4 frames) on their first frame when they start a shot. 6) Optional colour accent: the first emphasis phrase got a pink fill (#E28B8B, still difference) for the whole shot ('at my Prime').
emphasis_rule.stacked_variant: Use the left-anchored stacked block (script word + 2 sans lines with staggered blur-ins) for one short 3-word clause per video, starting on a shot cut ('They / don't / wanna').
emphasis_rule.normal_blend_variant: Use plain white Normal blend for the climax word and its follow-up when the shot is bright and celebratory ('Win', 'but i').

words.entrance: blur+fade in, 7 frames (f086-f092): opacity ~0.20,0.29,0.41,0.56,0.76,0.80,0.93 then 1.0; extra gaussian blur sigma ~3.9->0 px
blur+fade in, ~6 frames (f090-f095): opacity ~0.08,0.18,0.52,0.80,0.94,0.93 then 1.0; extra blur sigma ~6.3->0 px
blur+fade in, ~2-3 frames (f095-f096/97): opacity ~0.55 then 1.0; extra blur sigma ~3.4 -> 1.5 -> 0 px (a <=15% very blurred ghost may already exist f092-f094; unreliable)

renderer_recipe: 1. Per word: draw the text as a white (#FFFFFF) mask, anti-aliased, no stroke/shadow. Sans: Inter Display ExtraBold stand-in, 108 px (0.100*H), tracking -0.07 em, lowercase, centred, baseline at 0.537*H. Script: formal swash script, capitals ~250-272 px tall, centred.
2. Composite onto the footage with Difference: out = |fill - footage| (fill white -> 1-footage); pink #E28B8B fill for the 'at my Prime' shot; Normal white for 'Win'/'but i'.
3. Hard-cut words in/out on exact frames; next word appears on the very next frame.
4. Apply the shot's digital zoom to the composited frame (captions included), about the frame centre, exponential ease; punch-in +11..+13% (tau ~4 f) starting on each script word's first frame.
5. Stacked block variant: left-anchored, They/don't/wanna with 4-5 frame staggered blur(sigma 4-6 px -> 0)+fade(0 -> 1) entrances over 5-7 frames.
6. No glitch layer, no occlusion matte (optional feature only: the reference never occludes).
confidence_notes: Font families are not identified; Inter Display ExtraBold is a geometric stand-in (IoU ~0.87).

Opacity of words over near-black backgrounds cannot be distinguished between difference and normal numerically; they are assigned Difference by style consistency and by inverted bright objects where present.
They-block opacity/blur curves come from edge profiles over a busy, moving background (passers-by): +-0.1 opacity, +-1 px sigma. wanna before f095 is uncertain.
Absolute zoom level of each shot is unknown; only relative per-frame changes are measured (they are precise to ~0.2%).
